Subject: Pooling partial-token charges across microcalls and long-context sessions

Hi Kayla —

Thanks for sharing the Q3 invoice. I pulled a quick rollup and noticed a pattern that looks like the majority of the overage is coming from a large number of very short microcalls (health-check style queries and small metadata lookups) that each get rounded up to the billing quantum.

Short summary:
- Observed: ~120 microcalls/day averaging ~0.4 billed tokens each (after model tokenization) across several endpoints.
- Problem: current per-call quantum rounding bills many of those as 1 token, creating a large delta vs actual tokenized usage.
- Impact (sample): the example attached (novamed_invoice_q3.pdf) shows ~5,400 billed tokens from microcalls where raw tokenized sum is ~1,800.

Questions / options we can consider:
1) Short window pooling: aggregate partial-token usage for the same conversation/request owner within a configurable time window (e.g., 60–120s) and invoice the aggregated token count against the quantum once.
2) Conversation-based pooling: pool partial tokens per conversation id (or session id) until a threshold or explicit flush.
3) Monthly reconciliation: keep per-call charging for realtime metrics but reconcile and credit any rounding delta at month close when the pooled total is materially lower.

I attached a quick sample calc (pooling-sample-calcs.xlsx) that models a 60s pooling window vs current per-call rounding. If we pool by conversation-id for the microcalls you sent, the billed tokens drop substantially in the example.

Two asks:
- Kayla: can you confirm whether those microcalls are from one service account / conversation id or are they distinct session tokens? That determines whether conversation-based pooling is viable.
- Kimberly / Vanessa: if we agree on a pilot approach, can we propose a telemetry flag to seat through the pilot and a threshold for automatic crediting?

I can hop on a short call if helpful — available 2–4pm PT tomorrow.

Best,

- Most of these microcalls originate from a single service account (search-index health checks) but are initiated across several conversation ids because they run inside separate short-lived worker processes.
- We do have some long-running sessions (clinical-assistant flows) that rely on the per-request KV cache and long context; we want to be sure any pooling approach doesn't change how those are accounted for.

Kayla — copied the key points below and sketched a pragmatic approach that balances accuracy, SLA surface area, and billing simplicity.

Design proposal (pricing & billing):
1) Pooling window: implement an opt-in 90-second pooling window applied per (service_account, conversation_id) tuple. This keeps pooling tight enough to avoid conflating unrelated user flows but long enough to capture microcall bursts from worker processes.
2) Aggregation rule: sum raw tokenized usage in the window, then map to billing quantum (quantum = 1 token for your SKU) for the aggregated sum (i.e., floor/ceil per-account rules applied to the aggregate instead of per-call).
3) KV / long-context: NO change to how KV cache or long-context tokens are counted — those remain full-token accounted per-call; pooling only affects fractional-token microcalls where raw token < 1 quantum.
4) Reconciliation: at month end, compute the delta between what would have been billed under per-call rounding vs pooled billing; if pooled billing is lower, issue an automatic credit when monthly delta exceeds $50.
5) Pilot telemetry: enable a telemetry flag for Novamed that logs both per-call and pooled tallies (no invoice impact during pilot) for 30 days; after pilot, switch to pooled billing live and apply reconciliation credit for the pilot month.

Example math (attached spreadsheet mirrors this):
- Scenario A (current per-call rounding): 120 microcalls * 1 token quantum billed = 120 billed tokens.
- Scenario B (pooled 90s window): 120 microcalls aggregated -> raw sum = 48 tokens -> billed = 48 tokens.
- Net delta: 72 tokens saved (~60% reduction for microcall traffic in this pattern).

Operational notes:
- We recommend we scope the pilot to the two service accounts Kayla called out and capture request_id & conversation_id mappings for 30 days.
- Engineering will need to add a short-lived conversation_id forwarding for the short-lived workers (or we pool by service_account if conversation ids are ephemeral).

Next steps I propose:
- Mateo: send Kayla the pilot telemetry flag and the spreadsheet with session-id labeling.
- Kayla: confirm which service accounts to include and who in your FP&A should receive the pilot recon report.
- Vanessa: help coordinate legal/procurement for a short pilot amendment (one paragraph).

Happy to take a quick call to walk through the spreadsheet.
